To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the SIM-3 scheme is superior to the H.261 scheme for videophone sequences; 2) segmentation maps are useful in motion estimation; 3) the constant-acceler-ation model is superior to the constant-velocity model.

(1) block matching is a very good choice for motion estimation in the H.261 standard and in the SIM- 3 scheme; (2) segmentation-based motion estimation can lead to a better compression of video data than full search block matching, but it requires a good segmentation map that can be compressed at very low bit rates; (3) motion-compensated postprocessing can be a powerful tool for improving the quality of decoded video, especially when combined with motion compensation at the receiver.

(i) a more precise motion description is useful in very low bit-rate coding of video; (ii) segmentation maps are useful to describe motion in very low bitrate coding; and (iii) constant-acceleration models are better than constant-velocity models for motion compensation.
